A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Q-learning with Adjoint Matching and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original OGBench experiments covering offline RL, online fine-tuning, sensitivity analyses, and data-quality robustness, including full appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and reports revised QSM baseline outcomes in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The written method specification changes locally: Equation (18) replaces the SOC penalty coefficient 1/2 with 2/sigma_t^2, and the critic dispersion term following Equation (26) gains a 1/K factor. The lean-adjoint update and QAM-FQL/QAM-EDIT variants remain unchanged; these formula revisions do not establish changes to executed code.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 10 OGBench domains and 50 main tasks, including the same large datasets and action-chunking tasks. The noisy and stitch dataset scenarios are retained in v3 Appendix A rather than removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged; the baseline count changing from 8 to 13 corrects the description of existing comparisons. However, v3 Appendix E reports a modified QSM sampler using a DAC-style denoised-action estimate plus noise, replacing v1's stated standard sampling procedure. DAC's displayed denoising formula is also revised, without evidence that its experiments were rerun.

E3.justification: Table 5 revises QSM hyperparameters in five domains. For example, (tau, eta) changes from (10, 10) to (30, 30) for both antmaze domains and to (3, 3) for cube-triple. Training budgets, model sizes, tuning design, and evaluation coverage otherwise remain the same.

E4.justification: The existing data-quality analysis has revised QSM curves in Figures 4 and 7, including markedly different behavior on noisy puzzle and cube tasks. Its experimental questions and comparator roster are retained. The gradient-clipping, flow-step, ensemble-size, and temperature sensitivity analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 12 evaluation seeds, means with 95% confidence intervals from 5,000 bootstrap samples, and four seeds for hyperparameter tuning. Changes to numerical interval endpoints do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: QSM results are substantially revised across Tables 1-2 and the main, full-training, and robustness plots. Table 1 changes its aggregate score from 42 to 39, cube-double from 56 to 33, and antmaze-giant from 15 to 24, reversing its aggregate ordering with ReBRAC at 40. QAM's aggregate scores remain 44, 45, and 46. These are revised baseline results under changed reported sampling and tuning, not same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Several mathematical expressions are corrected: the running-cost gradient changes sign in Equation (11), Equation (18) receives the noise-dependent SOC weighting, and Equation (45) restores the exponential Boltzmann form. The CGQL derivation replaces Gaussian-noise expectations with conditional expectations, and the Linex threshold inequalities are reversed. Proposition 1 and its appendix proof are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: adjoint matching enables expressive, behavior-constrained policy optimization using critic gradients, with strong offline and offline-to-online results. No new central contribution or broader applicability claim is introduced.

C2.justification: v3 adds a hypothesis that modified QSM sampling helps because critic gradients are evaluated on actions more likely to be in distribution, while acknowledging the procedure's nonstandard nature. It also qualifies the CGQL intermediate-score expression as an approximation. QAM's existing support-mismatch and ill-conditioned-critic limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds explicit equations for QSM's modified sampling procedure, and Table 5 updates its domain-specific settings. These improve documentation of the reported baseline implementation. Hardware, software framework, training-cost information, and the code-access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds two Ankile et al. works to the discussion of residual action-space policies and explicitly credits DAC for the pessimistic critic backup. The diffusion-guidance discussion moves to Appendix C with its substantive positioning retained; duplicate Fang references do not represent additional distinct work.

P1.justification: v3 selectively reorganizes the paper by moving the guidance-related-work discussion, robustness subsection, and pseudocode into appendices. It shortens some prose and captions, updates acknowledgments, and replaces the preprint header with an ICLR publication header. Most narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from the main text to Appendix A, and Algorithm 1 moves to the pseudocode appendix. Several captions are shortened and surrounding pages reflow. The existing eight figures and seven tables retain their overall display formats; numerical and curve revisions are assessed separately.

improvement.justification: v3 improves mathematical consistency through corrections such as Equations (11) and (18), and makes the QSM implementation more reproducible through explicit sampling equations and revised settings. The gains are limited by an unupdated Section 6 statement that ReBRAC trails QSM, contradicting v3 Table 1's 40 versus 39. The core contribution and breadth of evidence remain stable.
